decision: The roster is a billboard plus rows (Rising in Seoul, Moments this week, Tokyo crossover, LA breakouts), the browse pattern popularized by video-streaming apps
why: Partnership leads scan for 'who's moving where' before they analyze; rows by market answer that at a glance, the billboard names the one thing to act on.
value: The moment of the week is one click from a campaign.

decision: Cards expand after 300 ms of hover intent (or at once on focus) to show a live equalizer, brand fit and Pitch/Open; equalizers only animate on the open card
why: Twenty animated equalizers would be noise and battery; animating the one you're looking at says 'this is live' where it matters.
alternative: Every card animates all the time.
value: Calm rows, a lively focus, and keyboard parity.

decision: Brand fit is a score with its parts shown (audience overlap, market match, tone, safety) against the portfolio's own brands (Maré, Maré Pay, Atlas)
why: A bare percentage invites argument; the parts are what a partnerships lead would defend in a pitch.
value: Pitches arrive with their reasoning attached.

decision: Pitch to brand drafts a simulated-AI pitch grounded in three signals with sources, and nothing is sent until a person approves
why: Outbound messages to brands carry reputation; the draft saves time, the approval keeps accountability.
value: Faster pitches without surprises (reply rate target [value]).

decision: Momentum and the fan-edit page count move with the world clock, so Roster, Intelligence and Distribution tell the same story at the same minute
why: A home screen that disagrees with the analytics one click away destroys trust in both.
value: One evidence trail across every Pulse screen.
